messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert triggered — latency-slo-routing policy saw rapid p95 breaches and automated reroutes between model-variants in us-west1 <-> us-east1. Suspected feedback loop. Paging on-call SRE (alex) and runtime (sam). Rule: p95 > 300ms for 3m -> force reroute.

Alex Chen: oncall here, looking now. paging logs + routing decisions.

Maria G: saw a small policy change rolled last night that tightened p95 threshold from 350ms -> 300ms for tiered routing. Might be the cause.

Priya S: customer-facing: several enterprise customers report 504-ish latency spikes and degraded throughput since ~10:12 PDT. No full outages but UX broken for streaming. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/slo/latency (link).

Sam R: pulling routing decision logs. Getting a lot of rapid policy flips where requests are rerouted to fallback variants that then have higher latencies -> triggers another reroute -> loop. Example snippet: 
```
[10:13:02] route_decision: user_req -> model-variant-a (p95=320ms)
[10:13:04] auto_reroute -> model-variant-b (p95=290ms)
[10:13:06] route_decision: model-variant-b degraded (p95=340ms) -> reroute back -> variant-a
```
Looks like KV cache cold starts + cross-region fallback are amplifying latency.

Alex Chen: can we disable automated reroute for the affected policy while we stabilize? I don't want the feedback loop to keep flipping.

Sam R: yes. Temporarily changing policy to manual failover and bumping p95 threshold to 500ms. Running command: 
```
redwoodctl routing update-policy --id slo-routing-2026 --auto-reroute=false --p95-threshold=500ms --scope=us-*
```
Applying now.

deploy-bot: Strategy change deployed to routing control-plane (commit sha: a1b2c3d).

Priya S: notifying impacted customers and support. Drafting a short status note.

Maria G: also pinning affected sessions to the original model-variant where possible to avoid cross-variant cold KVs.

Sam R: scaling up variant caches and increasing replication in us-east1 for the next 10 minutes: 
```
redwoodctl infra scale --pool=variant-b-eu --replicas=4
```
(doing a conservative burst).

Alex Chen: confirmed automated reroute is off. Monitoring for immediate re-flapping. If latency stabilizes, we'll re-enable with more conservative thresholds.

Noah K: I'm coming in for handoff in 20m. Alex, if you need to pass off before then say now.

Alex Chen: I need to step out in 12m for an urgent call. Noah, can you take the active pager and continue triage? I'll leave notes.

Noah K: taking pager. Key things to watch: p95 per-variant, route flip counts, and number of reroute events/min. Query: 
```
metrics.query("routing.reroutes", {window: "1m"})
```

Alex Chen: notes added to runbook: 
- disable auto_reroute for slo-routing-2026 (done)
- bump p95 threshold to 500ms (done)
- pin sessions to last-known-good variant when possible (in flight)
- scale KV caches in impacted region (in flight)
- notify customers + support (pri)

Priya S: sent customer notice: "We are seeing higher than expected latencies for generating responses. We have paused automatic reroutes while we stabilize and are scaling capacity. No data loss. ETA initial stabilization 30 mins." :email:

Sam R: monitoring shows reroute counts dropped from ~40/min to ~2/min after policy change. p95 across variants trending down from ~360ms -> ~220ms for most traffic.

Priya S: support templates updated. Routing incident severity set to Sev2.

Maria G: root-cause preliminary: overly-aggressive p95 threshold combined with cross-region fallback to cold-primed variants that had slower cold-starts. The auto-reroute heuristic didn't account for cold-KV penalties. We need a guard to avoid rerouting if target variant has < X KV hits warmed.

Noah K: accepting pager. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and coordinate rollback triggers. If reroutes > 10/min or p95 > 400ms for >10m, we escalate to Sev1 and run full incident bridge.

Sam R: adding a temporary guard: disable reroute to variants with kv_warmness < 0.6 in the routing-decider. Patch applied: commit bc9f.

deploy-bot: Patch bc9f deployed to routing-decider (canary 10%).

Alex Chen: thanks team — I have to jump. Leaving sudo to Noah for the rest.

Noah K: quick status at 10:45 PDT: metrics stable, reroutes suppressed, customer impact reduced. Continuing 1h watch. Postmortem owners: maria (policy), sam (runtime), priya (communications). I'll create the postmortem ticket.

Priya S: created incident ticket: INC-2026-4821 and linked support thread.

Maria G: action items added to incident board: 
- add KV-warmness check to reroute heuristic (P0)
- add hysteresis to p95-trigger (P1)
- run canary of policy change with traffic fraction gating (P1)

Sam R: follow-up: we'll also instrument per-variant cold-start penalty and include it in routing cost function.

Noah K: closing thread for now — monitoring continues. Will update if we see regression. :thumbsup:
